explanations: terra: The Book is declared to contain no doubt, matching the section's dictionary statement that what is muhkam admits no uncertainty.

luna: People say “إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ” when told not to spread فساد; their claim of repair gives a specific counterexample to the section's sound-work sense of صَلَح. | terra: When forbidden to spread corruption, the people claim they are only reformers; the false label tests what counts as genuinely sound work.

luna: The reply names them as corrupters while they do not perceive it; it completes 2:11 by separating claimed repair from actual soundness. | terra: God identifies those self-named reformers as the actual corrupters, policing the section's lexical boundary between islah and fasad.
terra: After making what is on earth for people, God turns to heaven and proportions seven heavens, extending taswiya to a layered structure.
terra: God distinguishes the corrupter from the reformer, ٱلْمُفْسِدَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِ, stating the precise lexical boundary behind salihat as sound, unreduced work.
terra: The scattered bones are raised and clothed with flesh before the observer's eyes, staging the damaged human body's skilled reconstruction.

luna: In the detailed debt-writing passage, God calls written terms “أَقْسَطُ” and “أَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَادَةِ” and nearer to removing doubt; it joins measured craft, uprightness and the section's claim that a sound work admits no suspicion.
terra: God forms people in the wombs however He wills, making the hidden human form a deliberate product rather than an unexplained appearance.

luna: The distinction between “آيَاتٌ مُّحْكَمَاتٌ” and ambiguous verses gives context to the section's dictionary claim that the muhkam admits no suspicion; the ayah preserves the distinction rather than equating every verse with that quality. | terra: Some verses of the Book are مُّحْكَمَـٰتٌ and form its foundation, using the root the section explains as secured against defect or doubt.
terra: Jesus shapes from clay the form of a bird and it becomes living by God's permission; khalq visibly retains its sense of measured forming.

luna: God says He does not allow any worker's work to be lost; this directly supports the section's contrast between rejected spoiled work and the lasting wage for sound deeds. | terra: God answers that He never lets the work of any worker be lost, عَمَلَ عَـٰمِلٍ, sharpening the section's play between the working part and enduring human work.
terra: “Humanity was created weak” places constitutional weakness beside the best conformation, preventing good workmanship from being mistaken for self-sufficiency.
terra: God commands that judgments between people be made with justice, anchoring the h-k-m root's craftsmanship metaphor in its governing sense.
terra: The Quran's lack of many inconsistencies is offered as evidence of its divine source, another fault inspection of a firmly made text.
terra: Reforming relations between people is one of the few kinds of private counsel praised, and doing it for God is promised a great reward; islah and ajr meet.
terra: Satan promises to command people to alter God's creation, making deformation of the Maker's finished work an explicit transgression.
luna: Hypocrites are assigned “الدَّرْكِ الْأَسْفَلِ” of the Fire; if 95:5's low return is read as final moral descent, this supplies a specific lowest-depth counterpart.

luna: The forbidden “الْأَزْلَامِ” are arrows used to seek a decision; they give the section's carefully straightened arrow a contrary use as a lot, though the Qur'anic arrows are divining arrows rather than a craftsman's tool. | terra: Seeking decisions by divining arrows is forbidden; the section's smoothed arrow is here bounded by an illicit purpose rather than faulty manufacture.
terra: “Who is better than Allah in judgment?” gives the direct rhetorical parallel to asking whether Allah is the wisest or firmest of judges.

luna: The arrow used for divination is a boundary against the section's measured, corrected arrow: a crafted instrument is turned to chance-seeking rather than skilled work. | terra: Divining arrows are called an abomination مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنِ; the carefully made arrow becomes the opposite of salih work through corrupt use.
terra: Game coming within reach of hands and spears supplies the Quranic setting for the very spear whose shaft the section imagines an artisan straightening.
terra: The deliberate killing anticipated by the spear test requires a livestock equivalent judged by two just people, adding exact equivalence and judgment to 5:94's spear scene.
terra: Bad and good are declared unequal even when the abundance of the bad impresses; quantity cannot turn defective output into sound work.
terra: God recalls Jesus forming a bird-shape from clay by permission, again separating skilled form-making from God's gift of life.
luna: God's word is complete in truth and justice and no one can change it; this concretely matches the section's ح ك م definition of securing something against فساد.
terra: Full measure and weight in justice are commanded without overburdening a soul, another direct formulation of straight, proportionate human work.

luna: God calls His way “صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا” and contrasts it with other paths; the section's straightened spear gives a physical counterpart to this straight course and its deviations. | terra: God's straight path is to be followed rather than branching paths, a line image that clarifies what it means for a life to stay straightened.
terra: The Prophet is guided to a straight path and an upright religion, transferring the section's physical straightness into an ordered life.

luna: The ayah says God created and formed humankind before commanding the angels to bow to Adam; it connects the section's well-made human to the dignity and response attached to that making. | terra: God says He created and then formed humanity before the command to prostrate, joining human making to bestowed rank.
terra: Iblis compares fire with the clay from which Adam was created, judging the finished human by raw material rather than the Maker's act.

luna: The command not to spread فساد “بَعْدَ إِصْلَاحِهَا” directly joins corruption to the opposite of repair, the root relation the section draws for صَلَح. | terra: People are forbidden to corrupt the earth after its repair, بَعْدَ إِصْلَـٰحِهَا, stating the section's islah–fasad boundary as a temporal reversal.
terra: Thamud skillfully carve houses from mountains yet are warned not to spread corruption, placing impressive workmanship directly beside fasad.

luna: Shuʿayb commands full measure and weight and forbids فساد on earth; this puts measured work and soundness opposite corruption, the same relation the section draws from خَلْق and صَلَح. | terra: Full measure and weight are commanded, and corruption after the earth's repair is forbidden; exact work stands directly between islah and fasad.
terra: Shuayb asks God to decide truthfully and calls Him the best of judges, a contextual parallel to surah 95's closing question.
terra: Moses commands Aaron to set matters right and not follow the path of corrupters, making reform the active alternative to spoiled communal work.
terra: Those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer are called reformers, and God does not waste أَجْرَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ.
terra: Humans fitted with hearts, eyes, and ears but failing to use them become worse than cattle, showing fine equipment morally degraded through nonuse.
terra: The divinely fixed count of twelve months is called the upright religion, bringing numerical order and q-w-m straightness into one ordinance.
terra: Some believers have mixed a sound deed with another bad one, presenting human output as a composite whose quality requires repair.
terra: Every hardship and step is recorded as a sound deed, because God does not waste the reward of those who do well.
terra: God appoints phases for the moon so years and reckoning can be known, making measured form serve a precise human function.
terra: The Quran cannot be fabricated, confirms what precedes it, and details the Book without doubt from the Lord: sound provenance and sound construction coincide.
luna: There is no change in God's words; this repeated formulation supports the section's claim that the muhkam is secure from alteration.

luna: In the contest with Moses, God declares that He does not set right the work of corrupters (“لَا يُصْلِحُ عَمَلَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ”); this directly joins عمل, إصلاح and فساد, the section's account of sound versus spoiled work. | terra: Allah does not make sound عَمَلَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ, the work of corrupters; amal, islah, and fasad meet in a single verdict on defective work.
luna: The next ayah says God establishes truth by His words even when criminals dislike it; it completes the contest in 10:81 and clarifies the fate of corrupted work against what God makes firm.
terra: The Prophet is told to wait until God judges, for He is the best of judges; the title marks the reliability of the final verdict.

luna: The section explicitly cites “كِتَابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ”; this ayah's firming then detailing of the verses is the Qur'anic example of ح ك م as work made secure. | terra: The Book's verses are أُحْكِمَتْ, made firm and then detailed, the section's explicit Quranic instance of work secured against defect.

luna: Heavens and earth are created, then human life is made a test of who is best in deeds; this joins divine making to the section's concern for the quality of human work. | terra: After mentioning God's creation of heavens and earth, the ayah says the test is which person is best in work, linking Maker and tested makers.
terra: What worldly workers manufactured is void in the Hereafter and what they did is false, a direct picture of output that cannot remain.

luna: Noah is told to construct the ship under God's eyes and inspiration; the ayah supplies another specific act of making, akin to the section's measured craft. | terra: Noah is commanded to manufacture the Ark under God's eyes and revelation, a created object made under explicit divine oversight.
luna: Noah builds the ship while his people mock him; this neighbor adds the response of denial to the craft scene, like the section's human forgetting the maker despite being carefully made.

luna: Noah addresses God as “أَحْكَمُ الْحَاكِمِينَ”; this repeats the exact judge-formulation named in the section's 95:8 discussion, now in Noah's plea about his son. | terra: Noah addresses God as أَحْكَمُ ٱلْحَـٰكِمِينَ, the exact divine superlative behind 95:8 in an appeal for sound judgment.
terra: Shuayb's address names his people's measuring and commercial work before commanding its repair in the following ayat.
terra: Full measure and weight are commanded and فساد in the earth forbidden, directly opposing accurate work to corruption.
terra: Shuayb says he desires only reform as far as he can, naming islah as the purpose behind correcting the defective measures.
terra: The blessed receive a gift غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ, not cut off, a nonlexical parallel to the unbroken wage of sound work.

luna: The command “فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ” turns straightness into a commanded stance; it connects the section's physical straightening to faithful conduct. | terra: The Prophet is commanded فَٱسْتَقِمْ كَمَآ أُمِرْتَ, to be straight as ordered, turning the artisan's straightening into a human stance.
terra: Good deeds remove bad deeds, treating sound human acts as work whose effect repairs earlier damage.

luna: The command to be patient is followed by the claim that God does not waste the reward of good-doers; it states the endurance of worthwhile work that the section's reward image implies. | terra: Patience is joined to the assurance that God does not waste the reward of the muhsinin, preserving the return on well-done work.
terra: Joseph's secure establishment in the land is followed by the maxim that God does not waste the reward of those who do well.
terra: Jacob is called the best of judges when the brothers resolve to await his permission or God's judgment.
terra: Joseph links reverence and patience to the rule that God does not waste the reward of the muhsinin, again protecting good work's wage.
terra: God knows what every womb bears, what it lacks or increases, and every thing with Him is by measure; hidden formation is governed by exact sizing.
terra: False partners are asked whether they created something like God's creation so the products became confused, testing maker-claims by comparable workmanship.

luna: The torrent flows “بِقَدَرِهَا,” while foam rises from it and from metal heated for ornaments or tools; the foam vanishes but what benefits people remains. This unusually close meeting of measure, worked material, rejected byproduct and lasting useful work illuminates the section's crafted object and sound work. | terra: Metal heated to make ornaments or tools throws off dross, while what benefits people remains; useful finished work is separated from rejected waste.

luna: This neighbor of the foam-and-metal parable distinguishes those who answer their Lord from those who do not and names their opposed outcomes; it completes 13:17's useful remainder/vanishing foam with a judgment contrast.

luna: The deeds of those who reject their Lord are compared to ashes scattered by wind; this gives a concrete image for work that cannot remain, opposite the section's sound work and lasting wage. | terra: The works of rejecters are like ashes scattered by wind, a product that cannot be retained or recovered when its result is needed.
terra: A good word is likened to a good tree with a firm root and high branch, giving sound output a structure that stands.
terra: The sound tree continually yields fruit by its Lord's permission, completing 14:24's image of work whose goodness remains productive.
terra: A bad word is an uprooted bad tree with no stability, a concrete reversal of the straightened, sound product.
terra: The earth is spread, stabilized, and made to grow every kind of thing in measured balance, مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ مَّوْزُونٍ.
terra: God's treasuries contain all things, but He sends them down only by a known measure; provisioning follows exact limits rather than accident.
terra: Human creation from ringing clay and molded mud identifies the raw substance that is later proportioned and enlivened.

luna: God announces a human to be created from sounding clay; this gives the section's artisan image a specific raw material and staged act of making. | terra: God announces the clay material from which He will create a human, setting up the proportioning and enlivening in 15:29.

luna: After the clay is formed, God says “نَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِي”; this marks the completion of the crafted body with a further divine act. | terra: God says He will proportion the clay human, breathe into him, and command prostration; the honored human follows the Maker's finishing act.
terra: Iblis refuses a human made from ringing clay and molded mud, repeating the error of overlooking divine proportioning after the material stage.
terra: Thamud carve mountain houses feeling secure, a durable-looking human product whose security does not survive moral corruption.
luna: God's way is “قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ,” while other ways deviate; this gives the section's straight-course image a concrete contrast with crooked direction.
terra: The one who creates is denied equality with one who does not, a concise boundary between the true Maker and a claimed one.
terra: The invoked beings create nothing and are themselves created, reversing maker and artifact to expose false claims of agency.

luna: God creates people, then some are “يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ”; this is a direct bodily reversal for 95:5's return downward, without requiring the section's other, rejected-work sense of رَدّ. | terra: Some people are يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ, returned to the most abject age, a direct parallel to the finely made human being returned low.

luna: People emerge from their mothers knowing nothing and are given hearing, sight and hearts so that they may be grateful; this shows the maker furnishing the human with capacities and a purpose. | terra: God brings people from the womb knowing nothing and equips hearing, sight, and hearts, a functional completion intended to produce gratitude.
terra: Animal hides become light tents for travel and encampment, showing the section's measured leather as material made into a fit human object.
terra: What people possess runs out while what is with God remains, and the patient are paid by the best they did; passing product and lasting wage are joined.
terra: Whoever does عَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًا in faith receives a good life and reward by the best of their work, uniting all three workshop terms.

luna: The Qur'an guides to “لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ”; this carries the section's ق و م straightness from crafted object into a rightly directed way. | terra: The Quran guides to that which is أَقْوَمُ, most upright; the q-w-m family transfers the section's straightness from a made shaft to a human course.

luna: “أَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ” and “زِنُوا بِالْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ” give the section's measuring and straightening a concrete ethical scene of exact measure. | terra: Full measure and the straight balance, ٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ, give a moral scene of exact measuring joined to straightness.

luna: The deniers ask whether they will be raised as bones and dust; the ayah makes the return of a finished body the issue. | terra: The objectors ask whether bones and crumbled remains can become a new creation, presenting the human product after apparent total failure.

luna: The answer challenges them to imagine becoming stone or iron; it sharpens the material problem of a maker restoring what has dispersed. | terra: They are told to become stone or iron, carrying 17:49's challenge to materials that seem still harder to restore to life.

luna: The answer is the One who created them the first time; this closes the making-and-return sequence that surrounds the section's human craftsmanship. | terra: Asked who will return them, the answer is the One who originated them the first time; first workmanship guarantees reconstruction.
terra: Iblis asks whether he should prostrate to one God created from clay, again treating material as grounds to reject the finished work.
terra: The children of Adam are honored and preferred over much of creation, supplying the elevated valuation from which being returned low becomes a fall.

luna: The revealed book has no “عِوَجًا,” crookedness; this is a direct textual opposite to the section's straightening of a spear and its account of defective work. | terra: The revealed Book is praised because no crookedness, عِوَجًا, was put in it, the textual counterpart to a shaft straightened without defect.

luna: The next ayah calls the book “قَيِّمًا”; it completes the prior claim of no crookedness with an upright, sound form, echoing the section's ق و م image. | terra: قَيِّمًا continues 18:1: the Book is not merely free of crookedness but set upright, like the workpiece after takwim.

luna: Earth's adornment is made a test of which people are best in deeds; it joins crafted appearance and the quality of action, while the ayah's own context emphasizes the test. | terra: Earth's adornment is itself made as a test of who is أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا, joining a beautified product to the quality of human workmanship.
terra: God will turn Earth's adornment from 18:7 into barren ground, setting a limit on even the beautiful product used to test human work.
luna: The ayah says none can change God's words; it repeats the section's firm, protected work theme in the context of revelation.

luna: God says He does not waste the reward of anyone who does good work (“أَحْسَنَ عَمَلًا”); this is another direct formulation of the section's sound work receiving a lasting wage. | terra: God does not waste the reward of one who أَحْسَنَ عَمَلًا; excellent workmanship, human work, and an undamaged wage meet in one sentence.
terra: The believing companion recalls that God made the man from dust and a drop and then سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلًا, finished him as a man.

luna: The ayah contrasts passing wealth and children with “الْبَاقِيَاتُ الصَّالِحَاتُ,” which are better in reward and hope; it states what endures from good work against what passes. | terra: ٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ are the sound deeds that remain and are better in reward, directly naming durable work.

luna: When the wall is about to fall, the traveler “فَأَقَامَهُ” (sets it upright); the section's root ق و م is glossed through straightening, and this is a specific act of repair that restores a structure.

luna: The wall protected treasure for two orphans until they matured, because their father was righteous; this later explanation completes 18:77's repair and links sound work to care and eventual benefit.
terra: A people identify Gog and Magog as corrupters and offer payment for a barrier, stating the defect and proposed wage before the sound construction begins.
terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn asks for strength to make a barrier, identifying purpose, labor, and intended function before the material process of 18:96.
terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn levels iron blocks between two sides, heats them to fire, and pours molten metal over them: a fully staged process of making sound work.
terra: The completed barrier cannot be climbed or pierced, so 18:96's careful process is vindicated by a product fit for its purpose.
terra: The flawless barrier of 18:96–97 will be leveled when God's promise comes, setting a boundary even on excellent human workmanship.
terra: The question introduces those greatest in loss with respect to their works, preparing an inspection of output that fails despite effort.
terra: Their effort is lost while they think they يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا, are perfecting workmanship; apparent good craft can be radically misjudged.

luna: Those who deny God's signs and meeting Him have deeds made fruitless; it parallels the section's rejected defective product, with the cause specified by this ayah's own context. | terra: Their works collapse and receive no weight on Judgment Day, the rejected product of 18:104 failing even the final measure.
terra: The human asks whether he will be brought out alive after death, voicing the objection that a ruined product cannot be remade.
terra: God answers by reminding the human that He created him before when he was nothing, making original manufacture the proof of repair.
terra: The lasting sound deeds are better with the Lord in reward and return, again identifying salihat as the work that survives.
terra: Moses is set on a course so that he may be made عَلَىٰ عَيْنِى, under God's eye, a close parallel to workmanship carried out with personal care.
terra: God tells Moses وَٱصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِى, “I fashioned you for Myself,” making a person both a crafted work and a work made for a purpose.
terra: Moses names the Lord as the one who gave each thing its created form and then guided it, joining construction to intended function.
terra: Exact scales are set for Judgment so no soul is wronged and even a mustard-seed weight is brought, applying flawless measure to the assessment of work.
terra: David and Solomon judge the damaged field, beginning a passage in which divine hukm is followed by David's taught manufacture of armor.
terra: Solomon is given understanding of the case and both prophets receive judgment and knowledge, bridging adjudication to the craft instruction in 21:80.

luna: David is taught to make armor that protects people in battle; it is a specific parallel to the section's well-fashioned spear and arrow as useful crafted objects. | terra: God teaches David the manufacture of armor that protects people, a concrete case of skilled work made sound by fitness for purpose.
terra: God says وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُۥ زَوْجَهُۥ, that He repaired Zechariah's wife for him, a Quranic instance of divine islah applied to a human body.
terra: A believer who does sound deeds has his striving neither denied nor lost, and it is written down, securing the work's lasting account.
terra: God promises to repeat creation just as He began it, explicitly treating the future body as a renewed first work.
terra: The plea “My Lord, judge with truth” identifies truthful adjudication as the governing sense alongside the section's firmness sense.

luna: While describing formation from dust through the womb, this ayah also names return to “أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ”; it supplies a bodily reading of the section's descent from the human's best form. | terra: The fetus passes through formed and unformed flesh, while some humans are returned to the most decrepit age; the same ayah holds formation and deterioration together.

luna: After Satan's interference, God “يُحْكِمُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ”; this directly develops the section's ح ك م branch as making something firm against corruption. | terra: After satanic interference is removed, God يُحْكِمُ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ, makes His signs firm, giving the root an active textual repair context.
terra: Those invoked besides God cannot create even a fly, exposing the absolute limit of rival makers against the craftsmanship attributed to God.

luna: The human's beginning is traced to an extract of clay, supplying the material stage for the section's image of measured material being worked. | terra: The human workpiece begins as an extract of clay, supplying the first material for the staged construction completed in 23:14.

luna: The extract becomes a drop placed in a secure resting place; this gives the human-making image an ordered intermediate stage. | terra: The drop is placed in a secure lodging, a controlled intermediate step between selected material and the transformed body of 23:14.

luna: The ayah traces successive formation through clot, lump, bones and flesh, then says “أَنشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ”; its closing “أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ” makes the workman's quality explicit. | terra: Successive fetal materials become bones clothed with flesh and then another creation; أَحْسَنُ ٱلْخَـٰلِقِينَ praises the maker after the whole process.
terra: Water is sent down in due measure and lodged in the earth, showing provision handled by the same deliberate measure as created form.

luna: Noah is commanded to build the ship under God's watch and revelation; this stages the section's human craftsman at work under divine direction. | terra: The repeated Ark command, “make under Our eyes,” reinforces the image of careful manufacture supervised by its true designer.
terra: God brings people forth and makes hearing, sight, and hearts for them, another functional inventory of the finished human.

luna: The ayah asks whether people thought they were created in vain and would not return to God; it gives a direct purpose-and-return counterpart to the section's crafted human and question about judgment.

luna: After saying God created all things, the ayah says “فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا”; creation and precise measure appear together, as in the section's account of measuring a hide before cutting. | terra: God created every thing and فَقَدَّرَهُۥ تَقْدِيرًا, measured it with exact measure, matching khalq as measuring material before the cut.
terra: God turns the deeds of the deniers into scattered dust, the fate of work that proves wholly unsound at inspection.

luna: After repentance, faith and righteous work, God replaces evil deeds with good ones; this is a specific repair of spoiled work, rather than a generic reference to good deeds. | terra: For the repentant believer who does sound work, God changes bad deeds into good ones, a moral refashioning of spoiled output.
terra: The people build a landmark on every height merely to play, exposing skilled construction whose purpose makes it vain.
terra: They construct strongholds as if they will live forever, turning durable workmanship into an illusion of permanence.
terra: Thamud carve houses from mountains with great skill, yet the surrounding rebuke makes virtuoso craft insufficient without sound conduct.
terra: The transgressing leaders are those who corrupt the earth and do not repair it, pairing both sides of the lexical opposition in one description.

luna: “أَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ” begins a passage on full measure; it directly echoes the section's hide measured before cutting and frames craft as work that must be sound. | terra: The command to give full measure and not diminish others turns accurate sizing into sound human work rather than a spoiled product.

luna: “وَزِنُوا بِالْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ” supplies a straight balance, joining the section's straight spear and proper measurement in one image. | terra: Weighing with the straight balance, ٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ, supplies the straight measuring tool for 26:181's command.

luna: The warning not to deprive people of their things or spread فساد completes the measured-work passage by showing what a defective, corrupt practice does to others. | terra: The measuring commands culminate in a ban on depriving people and spreading corruption, explicitly placing just work against fasad.
terra: Nine men in the city spread corruption and do not repair, another explicit pairing of fasad with the absence of islah.

luna: The mountains are described as a work of God who “أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ”; this is a direct formulation of the masterful finishing that the section draws from أَحْسَنَ. | terra: Moving mountains are called صُنْعَ ٱللَّهِ, the workmanship of God who perfected every thing; it makes divine creation an inspected, exact craft.
terra: Pharaoh commands clay to be fired and a tower built to challenge Moses' God, a carefully made artifact serving arrogant falsehood.

luna: The command “أَحْسِن كَمَا أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ” joins God's good work toward a person to that person's good work, then forbids فساد; it closely matches the section's crafted human, صالحات, and soundness against corruption.
terra: Believers who do sound deeds have faults removed and are rewarded according to the best they used to do.
terra: People are asked whether they see how God begins creation and then repeats it, presenting making and remaking as one competence.
terra: Travel through the earth is commanded to inspect how creation began, after which God produces the later creation.
terra: The spider's house is the frailest of houses; it supplies a natural image of construction that exists yet fails as reliable shelter.
terra: God begins creation and then repeats it before people return to Him, another concise cycle of making and remaking.

luna: God begins creation and repeats it, and the repetition is easier for Him; this directly links original making to restoration after decline. | terra: Beginning and repeating creation belong to God, and repetition is described as easiest for Him, denying difficulty in reconstructing the work.
terra: The addressee is told to set his face upright to the fitrah on which God fashioned people, with no altering God's creation; form and right alignment coincide.
terra: Corruption appears on land and sea through what human hands have earned; spoiled worldly conditions are treated as the product of human work.

luna: The sequence weakness, strength, then weakness again makes bodily decline a concrete reversal of the section's image of a human made in the best proportion. | terra: God makes weakness, then strength, then weakness and gray hair; the finished human product visibly passes back through loss of strength.
terra: After “this is God's creation,” challengers are told to show what others created, turning workmanship into visible evidence against false partners.

luna: The section's root خ ل ق is glossed through measuring material before cutting, and أَحْسَن as working something well; here God “أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ”, directly joining making and workmanship. | terra: God is the maker who أَحْسَنَ every thing He created; this directly states the section's sense of ahsana as finishing created work well.
terra: Human progeny is made from an extract of humble fluid, the material stage between 32:7's universal craftsmanship and 32:9's finishing.

luna: This continues the making process with “سَوَّاهُ” and the spirit, then gives hearing, sight and hearts; it shows the formed human as a deliberately furnished work. | terra: God proportions the human, breathes spirit, and installs hearing, sight, and hearts, continuing 32:7's good workmanship into functional completion.
terra: Believers are commanded to speak a straight, sound word, قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا, the human verbal counterpart to a straightened workpiece.

luna: Speaking rightly is followed by God's setting deeds right and forgiving sins; it directly connects sound speech, إصلاح of work and divine repair. | terra: God promises in response to 33:70 to يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَـٰلَكُمْ, repair their deeds, directly treating human outputs as corrigible work.

luna: God makes iron pliable for David; the next ayah directs him to make armor. This gives the section's spear-and-arrow craft a concrete Qur'anic scene of material shaped for use. | terra: Iron is softened for David before the measured armor-making command of 34:11, supplying the workable material on the divine craftsman's bench.

luna: David is told to make linked armor, measure its links (“وَقَدِّرْ فِي السَّرْدِ”), and do righteous work; this directly joins measured craftsmanship to صَالِحًا, the section's sound-work theme. | terra: David is told to make full coats of mail, measure the links, and do sound work; craft, exact measure, and صَـٰلِحًا converge in one workshop command.
terra: Molten copper is made to flow for Solomon and jinn labor under divine command, supplying material and workforce for the products listed in 34:13.
terra: The jinn make buildings, images, basins, and fixed cauldrons for Solomon, and David's family is commanded to work gratefully; product and amal share one workshop.
terra: Good speech ascends and sound work raises it, giving صالح work a direction and durability that corrupt output lacks.
terra: God measures the moon through stages until it resembles an old palm stalk, displaying form governed through a sequence of exact measures.

luna: The ayah says that one granted long life is “نُنَكِّسْهُ فِي الْخَلْقِ”; this directly pictures a reversal within the created form, one possible bodily counterpart to 95:5. | terra: Whomever God grants long life He reverses in creation, نُنَكِّسْهُ فِى ٱلْخَلْقِ, making aging an inversion of the original workmanship.
terra: Cattle are described as created for humans from what God's hands made, giving another direct divine-hand formulation for useful products.
terra: The disputing human forgets that God created him from a drop, setting up the decayed-bone challenge answered by 36:79.

luna: The objector asks who will give life to “الْعِظَامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ”; the broken, decayed bone recalls the section's dictionary branch for أَجْر as a fracture joining while the bone remains crooked. | terra: The human displays rotten bones and asks who can revive them, presenting the apparently ruined product whose Maker is named in 36:79.

luna: The answer points to the One who produced the bones the first time; it ties the section's crafted creation to the possibility of restoring what has broken down. | terra: The one who produced the bones the first time will revive them; first manufacture is the warrant for repairing the decayed product.

luna: Abraham asks whether his people worship what they carve; the section's human craftsman and crafted arrow meet here in a reversal where made objects are wrongly worshipped. | terra: Abraham asks whether people worship what they carve; the artisan's product becomes an object of worship instead of evidence of its maker.

luna: The ayah says God created the makers and what they make; it sharpens the section's boundary between human workmanship and the divine making of the human. | terra: Allah has created both the people and what they make, وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ, putting human makers and their products inside the greater Maker's work.
terra: Elijah asks whether his people abandon أَحْسَنَ ٱلْخَـٰلِقِينَ for Baal, applying the maker superlative in a direct worship contrast.
terra: The verb سَاهَمَ describes casting lots aboard Jonah's ship; it may preserve the lot-arrow scene, though the ayah does not itself name an arrow.
luna: The heavens and earth were not created in vain; the ayah calls that assumption the disbelievers' and links purposive making to the section's challenge about judgment.
terra: Those who believe and do sound deeds are set against corrupters on earth; righteous work and fasad are denied equal treatment.
terra: The announced creation of a human from clay supplies the raw material before the explicit proportioning in 38:72.
terra: The clay human is first سَوَّيْتُهُ, brought into proportion, and then given spirit, again staging form before completed life.
terra: God rebukes Iblis for refusing the one خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَىَّ; the wording puts the human's singular workmanship at the center of his dignity.
terra: Iblis answers 38:75 by judging fire superior to clay, reducing the honored crafted human to raw material and ignoring the Maker's finishing work.

luna: God creates people in their mothers' wombs “خَلْقًا مِنْ بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ”; the ayah makes the section's crafted form a staged, hidden process. | terra: People are made in their mothers' wombs as creation after creation in three darknesses, revealing the hidden staged workshop behind the finished human.
terra: The patient are paid their reward without reckoning, another formulation of a wage not clipped or exhausted.
terra: God sends down the best discourse as a mutually consistent, repeated Book; excellence here includes coherence throughout the completed work.
terra: The Arabic Quran is described as غَيْرَ ذِى عِوَجٍ, an artifact of speech without crookedness that calls its hearers to guard themselves.
terra: God removes the worst of what believers did and rewards them by the best of their work, preserving the well-made part rather than the defect.
terra: Pharaoh commands Haman to build him a lofty structure, repeating the scene of corrupt authority directing human workmanship.
terra: The tower's stated purpose is to reach the heavenly ways and inspect Moses' God, exposing the false aim assigned to the construction.

luna: Alongside earth made as a dwelling and sky as a structure, the ayah says God formed and beautified human forms; it extends the section's workmanship image to the ordered world around the human. | terra: Earth as a settled floor and heaven as a structure frame the statement that God formed people and perfected their forms.

luna: The ayah follows human formation from dust and drop through maturity to old age and death; that life course clarifies how a carefully made form can decline. | terra: Dust, drop, clot, childhood, maturity, and old age are one divinely managed production and decline sequence, illuminating both best form and its later reversal.

luna: Believers who do صالحات are promised “أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ”; this directly joins the section's sound works to its unending reward. | terra: Belief and sound deeds again lead to أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, confirming that the lasting wage belongs to work that remains sound.
terra: God places stabilizers and blessings in the earth and measures its sustenance in four days, making provision another deliberately measured work.
terra: Heaven is still smoke when God commands heaven and earth to come willingly, supplying the unformed material and obedience before 41:12's completion.
terra: The heavens are completed as seven in two days, each assigned its command and the lower one adorned and guarded; construction includes order and finish.

luna: Those who say their Lord is God and then “اسْتَقَامُوا” receive the promise of no fear; the section's straightness becomes a sustained human response to the maker. | terra: Those who say their Lord is Allah and then remain straight receive angelic assurance, showing what a human life held to its line yields.
terra: The best speech is attributed to one who calls to God and does sound work, combining the section's ahsan and salih language in a human output.

luna: Falsehood cannot approach the revelation from before or behind, which is from the Wise and Praiseworthy; the ayah gives a specific boundary against فساد for the section's notion of firm work. | terra: Falsehood cannot reach the revelation from before or behind, making the Book a secured work protected from corrupting intrusion.
terra: The call to religion includes “be straight as you were commanded,” another direct moral use of the section's line-straightness.
terra: Provision is sent down by measure because unlimited abundance would provoke transgression, showing measure fitted to the recipient's condition.
terra: One who pardons and repairs has his reward with God; islah and ajr are explicitly joined.
terra: Water is sent from the sky by measure and revives dead land, making calibrated provision productive and restorative.
terra: Holding firmly to revelation is joined to being on a straight path, making the sound Book the means of maintaining human alignment.
luna: The heavens and earth were not created in play; this states that creation is purposeful, a boundary against treating the section's crafted human as an accidental or useless product.
luna: The next ayah says they were created in truth, though most do not know; it completes 44:38 by naming the purposeful order behind creation.
terra: Evildoers cannot be made equal in life and death to believers who do sound deeds; سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ condemns that as defective judgment.
luna: God created heavens and earth in truth so that each soul is recompensed for what it earned; the ayah directly joins deliberate creation to measured recompense for work.
terra: The idolaters are challenged to show what their partners created of the earth, demanding an actual product rather than a claimed maker.

luna: This repeats “اسْتَقَامُوا” for those who affirm God and promises no fear or grief; it extends the section's straight-course image to steady conduct and its result. | terra: Those who affirm their Lord and then remain straight are freed from fear and grief, the parallel outcome of moral straightening.
terra: The mature believer asks God to make his descendants sound for him, extending divine islah across human generations.
terra: The Creator of heaven and earth did not tire in making them and is able to revive the dead, joining faultless first work to human restoration.

luna: For believers who do righteous deeds, God removes their evils and “أَصْلَحَ بَالَهُمْ”; this directly develops the section's note that ص ل ح includes God's setting the human right. | terra: Those who believe and do sound deeds have their evils removed and their condition repaired, وَأَصْلَحَ بَالَهُمْ; good work is answered by divine repair.
terra: Believers ask for a surah, but when a decisive or firmly established surah is sent the sick-hearted recoil; muhkam textual form tests its hearers.
terra: The sky is built, adorned, and found to have no fissures; beauty and structural soundness are one inspected piece of workmanship.
terra: God denies weariness in the first creation and points to a new creation, treating remaking as no defect or exhaustion in the Maker.
terra: God says He created the human and knows the soul's whisper, applying the maker's intimate knowledge to the interior of the product.
terra: The six-stage creation of heaven, earth, and what lies between caused God no weariness, excluding fatigue from the divine workshop.
terra: God says He built the heaven with might, supplying another direct cosmic construction scene for divine craftsmanship.
terra: God spreads the earth and calls Himself an excellent spreader, so the construction of 51:47 is complemented by a fitted floor.
terra: “Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?” forces humans to distinguish product from maker.
terra: The challenge expands from human self-creation to the making of heavens and earth, exposing the absence of any rival workshop.
terra: God repays those who do evil for what they did and rewards those who do well with the best, judging outputs by their quality.
terra: God knows people best both when He produced them from earth and when they were embryos in wombs, linking hidden formation to the Maker's knowledge.
terra: God creates the male and female pair, identifying differentiated human forms as products of one Maker.
terra: The pair of 53:45 is made from an emitted drop, revealing the modest material beneath the differentiated finished forms.

luna: The ayah says God created every thing “بِقَدَرٍ”; this directly parallels the section's dictionary gloss of خَلْق as straight, measured apportionment. | terra: Every created thing is made بِقَدَرٍ, giving the section's workshop measure a universal formulation.
terra: God's creation of the human opens a two-step statement whose next ayah supplies a fitted human capacity.
terra: Teaching the created human articulate expression shows the product completed with a distinctive working faculty.
terra: The sun and moon run by exact calculation, a cosmic parallel to the measured, dependable working part.

luna: God raised the sky and set the “مِيزَان”; the image extends the section's measured making from human craft to an order established by God. | terra: God raises the heaven and sets the balance, pairing cosmic construction with the standard by which things are kept proportionate.

luna: The command not to transgress the balance makes measured proportion a boundary against excess, complementing the section's straight measure. | terra: Humans are forbidden to upset the balance established in 55:7, defining a boundary against spoiling the Maker's measure.

luna: The command to establish weight in justice and not make the balance deficient states the opposite of flawed measure in the section's craftsmanship image. | terra: The command to establish weight justly and not diminish the balance makes exact measure an entrusted human imitation of ordered making.
terra: The human is made from dry ringing clay like pottery, bringing raw material and fashioned artifact together more explicitly than a generic creation statement.
terra: “We created you; why do you not affirm?” makes the finished human the evidence placed before the skeptical addressee.
terra: The hearers are made to inspect the reproductive material they emit, beginning the maker-versus-material inquiry continued in 56:59.
terra: The question asks whether people create the emitted material's human result or God does, locating true workmanship beyond the visible makers.
terra: Death is measured out among people and the Maker is not to be outstripped, establishing control over the finished body's end.
terra: God can replace people with their likes and produce them in a form they do not know, extending workmanship beyond the present form.
terra: Knowledge of the first creation is invoked as the reason to recognize the possibility of the further making in 56:61.
terra: The Book and balance establish justice, while iron supplies strength and human benefits; measure, judgment, and craft material converge in one divine provision.
terra: Fortified houses fail their owners and are ruined by their own hands and believers' hands, a dramatic unmaking of trusted human workmanship.
terra: The names Creator, Originator, and Fashioner occur together, distinguishing the maker's stages that the section unfolds as one workshop.

luna: This ayah says God created the heavens and earth in truth, then “صَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ”; its explicit good-forming closely matches the section's crafted human. | terra: After creating heaven and earth, God forms people and makes their forms good, فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ; workmanship and beauty are expressly joined.
terra: God has made for every thing a measure, قَدْرًا, generalizing the limits and exact sizing visible in the workshop image.

luna: God tests which people are “أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا”; the section's gloss of أَحْسَن as working a thing well helps connect crafted form to the quality of one's deeds. | terra: Life and death are created to test which person is أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا, shifting excellence from God's workmanship to the quality of human work.

luna: The sky is made in layers with no “تَفَاوُتٍ”; this reverses the section's dictionary example of a face whose defect turns the gaze away, presenting creation as free of mismatch. | terra: The seven-layered creation contains no disparity, and the viewer is told to return the gaze to seek a crack; divine work withstands fault inspection.

luna: The repeated gaze returns humbled after finding no flaw; the section's ر د د dictionary wording says ugliness can “يَرُدُّ الطَّرْفَ,” so this is a specific reversal in which the eye returns because the work is flawless. | terra: The gaze is returned twice yet comes back defeated and weary, completing 67:3's inspection of a product in which no flaw can be found.
terra: “Would the one who created not know?” reasons from the maker's intimate knowledge of the made thing, the stance assumed by the workshop image.
terra: One walking fallen on his face is opposed to one walking سَوِيًّا on a straight path, bodily abasement against upright human alignment.
terra: God brings people into being and makes hearing, sight, and hearts, another inventory of faculties fitted into the human product.

luna: The Prophet is told he has “لَأَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ”; here the section's uncut-wage phrase applies to the Prophet's labor, rather than specifically to believers' صالحات. | terra: The Prophet is promised أَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ, the same uncut reward that counters the section's dictionary image of a crookedly healed wage.
terra: God asks whether those who submit should be treated like criminals, posing the just discrimination that must govern the evaluation of human work.
terra: “How do you judge?” rebukes the leveling rejected in 68:35 and echoes the rhetorical challenge of 95:8.
terra: The human is said to have been created anxious and grasping, a moral susceptibility set against the body's best conformation.
terra: The praying are excepted from 70:19's created restlessness, paralleling the faithful workers excepted from humanity's downward course in surah 95.

luna: Noah says God created people “أَطْوَارًا,” in stages; this is a direct repeated formulation of the section's staged craftsmanship. | terra: People are reminded that God created them in stages, a compact statement of the successive workmanship elsewhere shown in the womb.

luna: The promise of abundant water is attached to people who “اسْتَقَامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ”; this gives a concrete consequence to the straightness motif, though the passage concerns a community's conduct rather than craft.
terra: Night worship is said to be أَقْوَمُ قِيلًا, more upright in speech; the q-w-m link is exact, but its relation to bodily workmanship is indirect.
luna: The question about gathering “عِظَامَهُ” directly brings bones into the resurrection discussion, echoing the section's bone-fracture dictionary image.

luna: God answers that He can proportion even the fingertips (“بَنَانَهُ”); this makes restoration a matter of exact forming, like the section's careful straightening and finishing. | terra: God can reassemble even the fingertips, making the finest bodily detail evidence of the Maker's exact construction and restorative power.

luna: The human is recalled as a drop of emitted fluid; this starts another Qur'anic account of material shaped into a person. | terra: The human starts as an emitted drop, establishing the unpromising raw material that 75:38 says God creates and proportions.

luna: The drop becomes a clinging substance and is then created and proportioned; the ayah gives the section's measured-making image a concrete sequence. | terra: The drop becomes a clot, then God creates and proportions it, فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ, compressing the workshop sequence into two verbs.

luna: After creation and proportioning, the ayah distinguishes the two sexes; it presents differentiation as part of the finished form. | terra: The Maker finishes the sequence by producing the male and female pair, showing that proportioning in 75:38 includes differentiated human form.

luna: The human is made from a mixed drop and furnished with hearing and sight for a test; the ayah connects careful formation to the capacities by which the work is judged. | terra: The human is created from a mixed drop for testing and then made hearing and seeing, joining raw material, purpose, and fitted faculties.
luna: God shows the way, leaving the human grateful or ungrateful; this makes the moral outcome of a well-made human explicit.

luna: The passage asks whether God created people from lowly fluid; this begins a direct account of material becoming human, alongside the section's خ ل ق gloss of measuring before cutting. | terra: The question points to humanity's creation from a humble fluid, opening the measured production sequence that ends at 77:23.

luna: The fluid is placed in a secure resting place; this is a specific intermediate stage in the making process. | terra: The material is put in a secure receptacle, an intermediate placement that makes the womb part of an ordered production process.

luna: The placement lasts to a known measure (“إِلَىٰ قَدَرٍ مَّعْلُومٍ”); it directly connects human formation to the section's measured making. | terra: The embryo remains until a known measure or term, إِلَىٰ قَدَرٍ مَّعْلُومٍ, supplying the exact limit praised in 77:23.

luna: The passage says God measured the process and calls Him the best measurer; this is a compact direct parallel to the section's reading of خ ل ق as straight measure. | terra: After the embryo is held until a known term, God says فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ ٱلْقَـٰدِرُونَ, praising the exactness of the measure.
terra: The question asks whether humans are harder to create than heaven and immediately says that God built it, turning creation into an explicit construction comparison.
terra: God raises the heaven's canopy and proportions it, فَسَوَّىٰهَا, so the building announced in 79:27 ends in exact alignment.
luna: The rebuke “قُتِلَ الْإِنسَانُ” introduces a human who forgets the maker; its next ayat ask what he was made from, making the section's craftsmanship a ground for accountability.
luna: The question “مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ” directly names creation, the root whose dictionary sense the section develops as measuring material before cutting.

luna: God's answer says He created the human and “فَقَدَّرَهُ”; the explicit apportioning gives the section's measurement-before-making detail a direct Qur'anic counterpart. | terra: From a drop God creates the human and then measures him, خَلَقَهُۥ فَقَدَّرَهُۥ, directly pairing creation with sizing.
luna: The ayah describes whoever wills to take “سَبِيلًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا”; it offers the same straight-course image that the section develops through the spear shaft.
terra: This identifies the addressee of 82:7 as the human deceived about his generous Lord, so the workmanship is presented as grounds against ingratitude.

luna: The section reads 95:4's خَلَقْنَا / تَقْوِيم as a maker measuring and straightening a human; this verse names the sequence خلق، فسوى، فعدل, so the artisan's careful proportion becomes explicit. | terra: The deceived human is confronted with the exact workshop sequence: God created him, then straightened and balanced him, فَسَوَّىٰكَ فَعَدَلَكَ.

luna: After fashioning and balancing the human, this ayah says God composed him in whatever صورة He willed; it completes the section's image of careful work reaching a finished form. | terra: This continues 82:7 by saying that the Maker assembled the human in whatever form He willed, identifying form as deliberate composition.
luna: After the creation and composition in 82:7–8, this ayah says people deny the Recompense; it completes the parallel to 95:4–7, where the made human is challenged about judgment.
luna: After the denial of recompense, the passage names guardians over people; this continues the parallel to the section by moving from fashioned humans to accountability for their deeds.
luna: The guardians are described as noble recorders; this specifies how deeds in the neighboring judgment passage are preserved.
luna: The recorders know what people do; this connects the section's عَمِلُوا صالحات to the accountability that follows the created-form passage.
luna: The passage says the righteous will be in bliss; it completes the preceding record of deeds with the good outcome that parallels 95:6.
luna: The passage says the wicked will be in Hell; this supplies the contrary outcome to the righteous and lasting reward in the section.
luna: The wicked enter the Fire on the Day of Recompense; this continues the judgment consequence that the section raises after the crafted human's descent.
luna: They are not absent from the Fire; this ayah specifies the permanence of the adverse outcome in the continuing passage.
luna: The passage asks what will make one know the Day of Recompense; it completes the warning after the created and composed human, matching the section's question about denial of judgment.
luna: The repeated question about the Day of Recompense intensifies the same warning, echoing the section's repeated challenge before God's final judgment.
luna: On that day no soul can avail another and command belongs to God; it closes the judgment passage with the sovereign decision that matches the section's final appeal to the best of judges.

luna: The passage condemns those who cheat in measure; this is the defective opposite of the section's measured hide and straightened tools. | terra: Woe is pronounced on those who defraud in measure, introducing a workshop standard deliberately bent in 83:2–3.

luna: The defrauders take full measure for themselves; the ayah specifies the self-serving half of the corrupt measuring scene. | terra: The defrauders demand full measure when receiving from others, showing a measuring practice corrupted by self-interest.

luna: They short people when measuring or weighing for them; this completes the concrete measure-and-defect contrast developed from the section's craft lexicon. | terra: When those same people measure or weigh for others they diminish, making defective measure the deliberate opposite of sound workmanship.
luna: The passage asks whether the defrauders expect to be raised for a great day; this neighbor connects corrupt measure to the judgment question that follows the section's making and work.
luna: The record of the wicked is placed in “سِجِّينٍ”; if the section's “أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ” points to final spiritual lowliness, this gives that descent a record and judgment setting.
luna: The record of the righteous is placed in “عِلِّيِّينَ,” a high counter-image to the section's low return and its exception for believers' sound works.

luna: The same promise, “أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ,” follows faith and صالحات here; it is a close parallel to the section's finished-work and lasting-wage claim. | terra: The full exception returns outside surah 95: believers who do sound deeds receive أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, an unbroken reward for sound work.
terra: God is the One who begins and repeats, a compressed formulation of the Maker's power to reproduce His work.
terra: The human is commanded to look at what he was created from, turning bodily origin into an inspection of the Maker's work.
terra: The gushing fluid supplies the answer to 86:5 and the raw material from which the human form is made.

luna: “خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى” directly joins creation to proportioning, the same careful forming that the section hears in 95:4. | terra: The paired verbs خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ present creation as making and then bringing the workpiece into sound proportion.

luna: “قَدَّرَ فَهَدَى” joins measured allotment to guidance; it makes the section's claim that making begins with right measure visible in another concise formulation. | terra: The Maker measures and then guides, وَٱلَّذِى قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ, so exact sizing is joined to fitness for purpose.

luna: After created proportion and measure, the pasture is made into dark stubble; this is a concrete created thing losing its flourishing form, a limited parallel to the section's best-made human being brought low.
terra: The punished faces are عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ, laboring and exhausted; effort alone has produced no sound or saving work.
terra: People are told to inspect how the camel was created, an invitation to infer the maker's workmanship from a finished creature.
terra: The same inspection asks how heaven was raised, shifting from creature to large-scale construction.
terra: The mountains are inspected for how they were set, adding stable placement to the sequence of created forms.
terra: The earth is inspected for how it was spread, completing the ordered environment in which the creature stands.
terra: Thamud cut rock in the valley, a repeated Quranic glimpse of forceful, skilled shaping of resistant material.
terra: The same emphatic wording, “We created the human,” ends with toil rather than best conformation, marking hardship as part of the crafted human condition.

luna: The human is given two eyes; this begins a list of fitted bodily faculties that makes the section's workmanship image concrete. | terra: God's making of two eyes identifies a paired, functional detail in the carefully equipped human body.

luna: The tongue and lips continue that list of formed faculties, each suited to the human's use. | terra: A tongue and two lips continue the inventory of fitted human parts, showing completion for speech rather than form alone.

luna: After naming these faculties, the ayah says God guided the human to two paths; it connects the fitted form to a choice between outcomes. | terra: After fitting the organs, God guides the human to two paths; made capacities carry a moral purpose and choice.

luna: The oath names the soul and “مَا سَوَّاهَا”; the same act of proportioning that makes the section's crafted human now frames the soul's moral possibilities. | terra: The oath by the soul and the One who proportioned it extends divine taswiya from the visible body to the inward human self.

luna: The soul is shown its wickedness and its piety; this explains the choice that follows a well-proportioned human form in the section's account. | terra: The proportioned soul of 91:7 is then shown both corruption and reverence, explaining why a well-made human can yield sound or spoiled work.
luna: “قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا” gives the soul's successful refinement; it concretizes the section's صَلَح branch as soundness rather than فساد.
luna: “وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّاهَا” supplies the contrary outcome to refinement, matching the section's contrast between sound work and corruption.
terra: The Lord creates the human from a clinging clot, a terse material image that makes the refined human's origin visible.
terra: Persistent rejecters are called the worst of created beings, the negative counterpart to 98:7's believers whose sound work makes them the best.
terra: Believers who do sound deeds are called the best of created beings, joining human workmanship to the final quality assigned to the human creature.
terra: The best creatures of 98:7 receive lasting gardens as their reward, so sound work again yields an enduring wage.
luna: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it; this makes the section's work-and-wage claim concrete at the smallest measure.
luna: The matching statement about an atom's weight of evil completes the exact accounting contrast between sound and spoiled work.
terra: Humanity is declared in loss, providing the same universal fall from a privileged human condition that surah 95 then qualifies by exception.
terra: The loss of 103:2 excludes those who believe and do sound deeds, closely matching the structural and verbal rescue in 95:6.
